Notes

Dear Giles Hugo,

Here’s the notes from your call with - Purchasing 0115 666 0551 on 25 September 2026 at 10:04:

The call involved Giles Hugo discussing ongoing projects, supplier competition, and upcoming orders with Brad from Exact Lasercut, focusing on delivery timelines, pricing, and quality issues. They also discussed potential future orders and improvements based on recent experiences.

Recap

  • Giles Hugo inquired about Brad's recent week and current workload, indicating a generally positive status and busy schedule.
  • Giles Hugo discussed a potential large order from a water jetting MD, awaiting a quote, and expressed preference to give the order to Brad's company if the quote is competitive, considering delivery speed and risk.
  • Brad confirmed he will check quantities and send a quote for 10 sets of the Forest Road lift, which Giles Hugo identified as a potential bread-and-butter product.
  • They discussed the possibility of ordering multiple sets to assess cost savings and Brad agreed to provide a quote for 10 sets based on the most recent order ending in 1597.
  • Giles Hugo emphasized the importance of competitive pricing and suggested starting with smaller orders to evaluate supplier performance before larger commitments.
  • They reviewed a previous order of 16mm sheets that was successfully delivered, indicating good past experience.
  • The conversation touched on a quality issue with aluminium strips at 28mm, caused by sheet distortion due to thinness and length, which Jamie suggested mitigating by increasing part clearance and avoiding sheet edges.
  • Brad acknowledged the issue and agreed to implement the suggested adjustments to prevent recurrence.

Tasks

  • Brad will check the quantities for 10 sets of the Forest Road lift and send a quote to Giles Hugo.
  • Brad will review the recent order details ending in 1597 to prepare the quote for 10 sets.
  • Brad will implement increased part clearance and avoid cutting near sheet edges to prevent aluminium strip distortion.
